title: Beni Mellal city and foothills, 16 Jul to 21 Aug 2026
summary: From 16 Jul to 21 Aug 2026 the radar shows 1.21 km2 turning brighter and 1.36 km2 darker in HV around Beni Mellal, much of it on the changing fields. Mean HH over the 6 km circle rose by 0.47 dB, built-up land included.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 36 days mean HV moved by 0.06 dB. In HV, 1.21 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 1.36 km2 darker; in HH, 1.9 km2 turned brighter and 1.03 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields had 0.66 km2 brighter and 0.93 km2 darker in HV, with a mean HV change of -0.75 dB. Built-up land, which should be stable, rose 0.53 dB in HH. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes rose 0.34 dB in HH and rough dry ground and fields 0.39 dB.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the darker fields: late summer harvests; harvest records would confirm it. Possible cause for the brighter fields: early sowing; a field visit would check it. Possible cause for the HH rise, built-up land included: a small calibration difference between the acquisitions; stable targets on more dates would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: A farm office could match the darker plots with its harvest records. Treat the HH rise as uncertain until stable targets confirm it.
